text: In therapy sessions, being too analytical can be a way of getting away from a feeling: you start explaining it as soon as it comes up, or you agree with the therapist just to get past it. If that keeps happening, look for someone trained in Intensive Short-Term Dynamic Psychotherapy, which I go into in my somatic guide's section [Can't Stay With a Feeling?](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/cant-stay-with-a-feeling). If instead you start to feel unreal, stop for the day, as [Dissociating or Unreal?](#§dissociating-or-unreal) says.
reader: an adult who keeps explaining feelings away, in the practice and in therapy sessions, deciding whether to look for a therapist trained for that

checked.point: ISTDP points out avoidance as it happens and turns the patient back toward the feeling; anxiety about the feeling drives the avoidance; the therapist watches it in tense muscles, sighing and foggy thinking; most patients have low anxiety tolerance and get a graded, slower format
checked.still_needed: yes: they picture a session and know they won't be pushed past what they can take

placement: a paragraph of its own at the end of "Too Analytical?", after: Whatever it is, just do it.
